Chapter One: When the World Changes Overnight—A Child’s Life in Haiti
Sometimes, life flips upside down in the blink of an eye. If you were in Haiti back in 2010, you probably remember exactly where you were when the earthquake hit. The ground shook, buildings crumbled, and suddenly, nothing felt safe or familiar.
But even as devastation swept through the city, something else quietly took root—resilience. People found ways to keep going, even when it seemed impossible.
Picture a small orphanage just outside Port-au-Prince. Its courtyard, surrounded by cracked walls, echoed with the sound of children’s laughter. In the middle of it all was a little girl—her hair tied up in bright ribbons, her eyes always darting around, searching for excitement. She’d lost her mother during childbirth and her father in the chaos that followed the quake.
Like so many others, she landed in this orphanage, where adults worked hard to make things feel a little more normal—even if the world outside stayed unpredictable.
The orphanage wasn’t just a shelter. It became a patchwork family, sewn together by necessity and genuine kindness. The kids shared everything: meals, toys, even the stories of the families they’d left behind. The adults—some from nearby, some from faraway places—did whatever it took to keep hope alive. They patched up walls, organized lessons, and tried their best to shield these kids from the world’s harsh edges.
Our little girl stood out. She was always the first to challenge the rules, the loudest voice in any game, and never afraid to ask tough questions that made the grown-ups stop and think. Her energy was infectious, and her laughter could brighten even the darkest room. Still, underneath all that boldness, she carried a quiet wish—a hope to belong somewhere, to have a real family of her own.
You know, most people don’t realize just how much children notice—especially in times like these. They see the worry hidden in the adults’ eyes, feel the tension when supplies start to run low, and sense the fear that lingers after every aftershock. But they also catch the small moments of love: a gentle hand on a shoulder, a meal shared between friends, or a bedtime story whispered in the dark. These little things become the building blocks of their strength.
As weeks turned into months, the orphanage became more than just a roof over their heads. It was a place to heal, to trust, and to find joy in the middle of so much loss. The children, especially our brave little girl, learned to hope again—even when everything had changed.
Her curiosity and stubborn spirit turned her into a symbol of hope, not just for the other kids, but for everyone around her. She showed that even in the toughest times, the human spirit has a way of shining through.
